title: Man. Post. Cap. II: Placeus denies strict poena; Fathers/Calvin by similitude
pass_a_gloss: But I denied that it is such a penalty in the Theses, and I cannot obtain from my conscience that I should not deny it even now. I know this corruption or concupiscence is called a penalty by the Fathers, and also somewhere by Calvin, but I deny it in a sense so proper, so strict. But on account of a certain likeness the name of penalty is accommodated to it. For as penalty follows fault and coheres with it, so hereditary corruption followed the fault of Adam and was born from it.
pass_b_english: In the Theses I refused to count it that sort of penalty, and conscience still will not let me reverse that denial. The Fathers do call this corruption—or concupiscence—a penalty, and Calvin does in places; I do not deny the word, only the so-proper, so-strict sense. The name rides on likeness. Penalty tracks fault and clings to it; hereditary corruption likewise tracked Adam's fault and sprang from it.
source_text: Ego vero talem esse poenam & negavi in Thesibus & non possum impetrare a conscientia mea ut nunc quoque non negem. Scio hanc corruptionem seu concupiscentiam poenam a Patribus appellari, necnon alicubi a Calvino, sed nego sensu ita proprio, ita stricto. Sed ob similitudinem quandam poenae nomen ei accommodatur. Ut enim poena sequitur culpam & cum ea cohaeret, sic corruptio haereditaria secuta est culpam Adami atque ex ea nata est.

choices.choice: Keep Theses denial + Fathers/Calvin name by likeness
choices.why: Placeus core denial of propriissime poena
